Native engine: several mediators and weights

Source: vignettes/articles/model-native-multi.qmd

Serial and parallel mediators, and sampling weights, with the native engine. Part of the Models collection; the last of four native engine pages. The engine is experimental.

Structure serial (a chain) or parallel mediators written as syntax
Route fit_sem(), then extract_mediation(fit, mediator = c(...), outcome = )
Classes returned SerialMediationData or ParallelMediationData
Weights fit_sem(weights = , se_type = "sandwich")

Not fit_mediation(engine = "native")

fit_mediation(engine = "native") takes one mediator and stops with “Must have length 1” for more. For several, fit with fit_sem() and extract.

library(medfit)

Attaching package: 'medfit'
The following object is masked from 'package:stats':

    decompose
library(generics)

Attaching package: 'generics'
The following objects are masked from 'package:base':

    as.difftime, as.factor, as.ordered, intersect, is.element, setdiff,
    setequal, union
covs <- "covariate1 + covariate2"

Serial mediators 

serial_syntax <- paste0("
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + ", covs, "
  mediator2 ~ d * mediator1 + a2 * treatment + ", covs, "
  outcome ~ b * mediator2 + b1 * mediator1 + cp * treatment + ", covs)
sfit <- fit_sem(serial_syntax, mediation_demo)
xs <- extract_mediation(sfit, treatment = "treatment",
                        mediator = c("mediator1", "mediator2"),
                        outcome = "outcome")
class(xs)[1]
[1] "medfit::SerialMediationData"
c(chain = unname(nie(xs)), every_path = unname(nie(xs, type = "total")),
  total = unname(te(xs)))
     chain every_path      total
0.07545039 0.36740438 0.53856776

With the default structure = "auto", medfit classifies the mediators from the model: here it finds the path from mediator1 to mediator2 and returns the serial class. See Serial mediation for what the three numbers mean.

Parallel mediators 

parallel_syntax <- paste0("
  mediator1 ~ a1 * treatment + ", covs, "
  mediator2 ~ a2 * treatment + ", covs, "
  outcome ~ b1 * mediator1 + b2 * mediator2 + cp * treatment + ", covs)
pfit <- fit_sem(parallel_syntax, mediation_demo)
xp <- extract_mediation(pfit, treatment = "treatment",
                        mediator = c("mediator1", "mediator2"),
                        outcome = "outcome", structure = "parallel")
class(xp)[1]
[1] "medfit::ParallelMediationData"
tidy(xp, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE)
# A tibble: 3 × 5
  term  estimate std_error conf_low conf_high
  <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
1 nie      0.367    0.0604   0.249      0.486
2 nde      0.171    0.106   -0.0366     0.379
3 te       0.539    0.114    0.315      0.762

Sampling weights

weights gives weighted maximum likelihood; pair it with se_type = "sandwich" for robust standard errors. The weights below are random, only to show the call:

set.seed(1)
w <- runif(nrow(mediation_demo), 0.5, 2)
wsyntax <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
  ab := a * b
"
wfit <- fit_sem(wsyntax, mediation_demo, weights = w, se_type = "sandwich")
wfit@defined
  name  expr       est         se
1   ab a * b 0.3450729 0.07052234

The scale of the weights does not matter. Supplying weights with the default se_type = "model" prints a once-per-session message that model-based standard errors are not valid under inverse-probability weighting.

Limits

  • fit_mediation(engine = "native") takes one mediator (see the warning above).
  • Four-way decomposition needs one mediator and a treatment-by-mediator product (x:m) in the outcome equation, and a model with a product cannot have a residual covariance between the mediators (parallel mediators with m1 ~~ m2 and a product are not supported; see product terms). Intercepts are estimated; see the native model page.
  • The native sandwich is the HC0 type, with casewise scores; the glm engine’s sandwich is HC3. They are different estimators, so the standard errors need not match.
  • The sandwich treats observations as independent, so it does not handle survey clusters, strata or replicate weights.
